subject: Embeddings pricing: dimension billing, per-vector vs per-token & EU discount
messages:
From: Marco Silva <marco@nexalytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick question on embed pricing and EU hosting

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the intro last week. We're sizing a pilot for an intent-classification+semantic-search feature and evaluating embeddings cost. A couple quick asks so we can estimate:

- How do you bill embeddings for models that support variable vector dimensions? Specifically, if we upload 4096-d vectors derived from a fine-tuned model, is that billed per-vector, or per-token-equivalent?
- Do you have a different unit definition for 1536 vs 4096 dimensional outputs?
- We're EU-first (data residency + GDPR). Can we get baseline hosted API pricing with EU region commitment options and any available discounts for a 12-month committed volume?

Rough target first-year volume: 150M vectors (mix of 1536/2048/4096). If possible, can you send a baseline ratecard and any short note on supported models (Redwood/canonical open models) for high-dim embeddings?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Marco
Marco Silva
Head of Platforms, Nexalytics
marco@nexalytics.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marco Silva <marco@nexalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick question on embed pricing and EU hosting

Hi Marco — great to hear from you, and congrats on moving to pilot. TL;DR: embeddings are billed per-vector unit; dimensions affect the unit multiplier. Details below and I attached a short matrix.

- Unit definition: we bill by "embedding units" (EUs). Base EU = one 1536-d vector. For other dims we apply a dimension multiplier: 2048-d = 1.33x EU, 4096-d = 2.67x EU. This keeps pricing predictable across dims.
- Per-token vs per-vector: embeddings are not billed per-token. Generation/token pricing is separate. The EU approach covers storage & compute amortized across requests.
- Model support: our hosted catalog supports Redwood-open-embed-1536, rdx-embed-2048, and rdx-embed-4096 (and a few third‑party open checkpoints). We'll include a compatibility table in the attachment.
- EU commitments: we offer a committed EU volume with region pinning. For a 12-month, 150M vector-equivalent commit (assuming your mix), we can discuss a stepped discount schedule — typically 15–25% off list depending on firm volumes and payment terms.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I'll share a baseline ratecard & model compatibility sheet (attached).
2) If you like the baseline, we can spin up a two-week pilot with a capped usage credit and EU-hosted endpoints to validate latency.
3) Ben (copied) will share commercial terms and a sample contract for procurement.

I attached: embed_pricing_matrix.xlsx (billing multipliers + model list) and a draft ratecard PDF (Nexalytics_v1_ratecard_draft.pdf). Let me know if you prefer the numbers split per-EU vs per-vector.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick question on embed pricing and EU hosting

Marco — putting rough commercials here so procurement has something to start with. These are baseline placeholders (final numbers subject to legal/finance approval):

- List: $0.00040 per EU (base 1536).
- 2048 multiplier 1.33x -> $0.00053 per EU-equivalent.
- 4096 multiplier 2.67x -> $0.00107 per EU-equivalent.
- 12‑month, 150M-vector commit (mixed dims) -> proposed blended price $0.00032 per EU (approx 20% off list) with EU-region pin and 30‑day SLA credits.

We can provide a redline of the commercial SOW and a DocuSign link after you confirm leadership approval. Also: for high-dim vectors we recommend enabling prefix caching on reads and a short TTL for hot vectors — reduces cost and improves latency.

Ben Carter

ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marco Silva <marco@nexalytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 14:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick question on embed pricing and EU hosting

Thanks Laura/Ben — that multiplier model makes sense. A couple follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

- Procurement: can you confirm whether the commit discount is applied to EU-equivalents after multipliers, or to raw vector counts? We need clear invoicing logic.
- Engineering: are the rdx-embed-4096 embeddings generated server-side by Redwood or do we bring our own vectors (we will likely push precomputed vectors)? If precomputed, any restrictions on quantization (int8/float16) for storage & retrieval?
- Privacy: we need confirmation that EU-hosted endpoints keep no customer vectors in shared caches outside the pinned region.

If you can send a short note addressing the three bullets above (invoicing line item example, precompute + quantization policy, data residency), procurement is happy to move forward.

—Marco
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marco Silva <marco@nexalytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@nexalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:42:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on embed pricing and EU hosting

Marco — answers inline and attached a one-page invoicing example.

1) Invoicing logic: commits and discounts are applied to "EU-equivalent" units after the dimension multiplier. Example line item (attached): 100,000 raw vectors (mix: 40% 1536, 40% 2048, 20% 4096) -> EU-equivalent = 100k*(0.4*1 + 0.4*1.33 + 0.2*2.67) = 133,400 EUs. Discount applies to the EUs. We'll include the calculation on each invoice for transparency.

2) Precomputed vectors & quantization: you can bring precomputed vectors. Supported storage formats: float32, float16, int8 (with provenance header). We do not re-encode uploaded vectors server-side except optional lossless compression. If you send int8, we'll bill based on the declared dimension multiplier (we treat quantization as a storage/compute optimization and do not apply additional discounts). We recommend providing a short checksum/provenance file so our ingestion can verify shape and checksum.

3) Data residency: EU-hosted endpoints pin storage and inference to EU regions. We do not replicate customer vectors to non-pinned regions unless you enable cross-region failover. Caching: short-lived in-memory caches exist on serving nodes in the region only; we never persist caches to shared global storage. We'll include the standard data-residency addendum in the SOW.

Next steps: Ben, can you get a sample SOW + payment terms draft into DocuSign? Marco/procurement — once SOW draft looks ok we'll provision EU-hosted pilot and apply a $10k pilot credit to validate throughput/latency.

Thanks — Laura

Attachments: Nexalytics_v1_ratecard_draft.pdf, embed_pricing_matrix.xlsx, invoicing_example_nexalytics.pdf
